processing: A cultivar, not a finished tea. It is described as suited to green tea, and it has been tested for machine-picked summer and autumn leaf for Tibetan-style dark tea.
harvest_season: Trials looked at machine picking in summer and autumn; a spring picking is not specifically recorded, though Sichuan green tea typically starts in early spring.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea made from it; no description is recorded.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Sichuan green tea: a clear yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Typical of Sichuan green tea: soft green leaf.
taste_profile: Made as green tea it is described as rich, fresh and smooth with a long-lasting floral aroma.

brewing.notes: A general method for green tea; a tea from this cultivar should be brewed for its style.

vintage_note: Rarely if ever sold under the cultivar name. Nothing specific is recorded; as with other Sichuan greens, green tea from it would normally be sold as the current spring's harvest, while dark tea would follow the rules of its own class.
description:
Mengshan 9 is a clonal tea cultivar selected from the Mengshan tea population at Mingshan near Ya'an in Sichuan. It is a diploid shrub, suited to green tea.

A Sichuan Agricultural University trial in the Yibin area compared 17 cultivars for machine picking in summer and autumn. Mengshan 9 gave significantly more fresh leaf than the Fuding Dabai control, and its machine-picked leaf also scored well for tenderness, evenness and intactness.

That makes it a practical plant for growers more than a name for drinkers. If a seller names it, ask what style was made from it.
history:
Selected from the Mengshan tea population by single-plant selection between 1976 and 1988, by the Mengshan Tea Farm in Mingshan County, Sichuan Agricultural University and the farm administration bureau of the Sichuan provincial agriculture department. It was certified as a provincial improved variety by Sichuan's crop variety committee in 1989.

A field trial published in 2024 recommended it for machine picking in summer and autumn and for planting in the Ya'an Tibetan tea area.
